posts.text:
Tito once dreamed of a South Slavic superstate stretching from the Alps to Bulgaria — a country that would have swallowed three modern nations whole.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ By the late 1940s, communist Yugoslavia and communist Bulgaria were negotiating a full political union — a South Slavic federation that would have run from Slovenia to the Black Sea.
2/ Tito's version went further still: a 'Balkan Federation' pulling in Albania too, plus a rump communist Greece if the Greek Civil War had gone the other way for the communist side.
3/ The map would have erased today's borders between Yugoslavia, Bulgaria and Albania, uniting roughly 25 million South Slavs and Albanians under one red flag for the first time in history.
4/ It collapsed almost entirely because of one man: Stalin. Moscow saw a Balkan federation as a rival power bloc it couldn't fully control, and pressured Bulgaria to back out.
5/ Then Tito broke with Stalin outright in 1948 — the Tito-Stalin split — and the whole federation idea died with the friendship. Yugoslavia went its own non-aligned way instead.

6/ Decades later, in the 1990s, Yugoslavia didn't expand — it violently split into seven countries. The union Tito once tried to build in one direction unraveled completely in the other.

What other Cold War mergers almost happened? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
